setup: Set the bar in the rack at upper-chest height
Bar on your upper back, not your neck
Balls of your feet on a plate or block
Set the safety arms just below the bar
execution: Let your heels sink for a stretch
Push through the balls of your feet
Rise as high as you can and pause
Lower slowly; no bounce at the bottom
faults: Don't bounce out of the bottom
Don't lean forward over your toes

notes: Work inside a rack with the safety arms set just below the lowest point the bar reaches, so you can set it down if you lose balance.
Use a stable, non-slip block or plate under the feet, and start light until your balance is steady.
If balance limits the load, a calf-raise machine or Smith machine takes it away.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Bodyweight calf raise
regressions.reason: Same movement with no bar; learn the full range and balance first.

regressions.name: Standing calf raise (machine)
regressions.reason: The machine takes away balance, so the calves are the only limit.

progressions.name: Single-leg calf raise
progressions.reason: One leg at a time with a dumbbell or a hand on the rack; much harder at the same load.

substitutions.name: Standing calf raise (machine)
substitutions.reason: Same straight-knee movement; stack or plate loading.

substitutions.name: Seated calf raise
substitutions.reason: Bent knees shift more work to the lower calf (soleus); weight added on the machine.

substitutions.name: Smith machine calf raise
substitutions.reason: Same movement with the bar on a guided track, so balance is easier.

substitutions.name: Leg-press calf raise
substitutions.reason: Calves only, with the back supported.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at knee-to-hip height so the ankle and the heel's travel below the block are clear. Bar seen end-on on the upper back. Rack uprights optional.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall with the bar on the upper back, knees soft. Balls of the feet on the edge of a block, heels dropped below it for a calf stretch.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Heels raised as high as possible, weight over the balls of the feet. Body rises straight up as one piece; no forward lean.

guideBrief.barPath: Straight up and down over the middle of the foot
emphasise: Heels drop below the block, then rise high
Only the ankles move; knees stay soft
Pauses at the top and at the stretch

sources.title: Motra exercise library: Barbell Standing Calf Raise
